title.value: Histology-informed automatic parcellation of white matter tracts in the rat spinal cord
title.justification: The title reflects the primary focus of the paper, which is on creating a method for automatic parcellation of white matter tracts in the rat spinal cord.
title.quote: Histology-informed automatic parcellation of white matter tracts in the rat spinal cord

extractions.description: The paper discusses an automatic parcellation method for white matter tracts in the rat spinal cord using axon morphometric data derived from scanning electron microscopy images. The approach utilizes histology-informed clustering and aims to provide a detailed anatomical map that can be used for better understanding white matter structures and potentially aid in medical diagnoses and treatments.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper's primary focus is on neuroanatomical research and the development of a method for mapping white matter tracts, which does not directly relate to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Knowing where these tracts are located in each individual is important for understanding the cause of potential sensorial, motor or cognitive deficits and for developing appropriate treatments.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on neuroanatomy and does not address topics related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: The objective of this study was to generate automatic parcellation of the rat spinal white matter tracts using the manifold information from scanning electron microscopy images of the entire spinal cord.

secondary_categories.justification: The research does not cover secondary themes related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.

applications.quote: Results show that axon morphometrics provide sufficient information to automatically identify some white matter tracts in the spinal cord, however, not all tracts were correctly identified.
